title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No real mathematical error. φ_x being an isomorphism needs T path-connected; this is included in '1-connexe'.
π should be read as the profinite completion π̂_1(X;T), since the f, g elements live in profinite groups. The notation silently switches.

The identification f ↦ φ_x^{-1}, g ↦ φ_y^{-1} giving the same element relies on the passage formula (9), presumably f_l(u) = l^{-1}(g_l(u)). This is consistent with conjugation by l_{y,x} matching φ_y φ_x^{-1}. The check is correct but left implicit.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at a simply connected subspace T → X (instead of at a point), giving a transitive system of identifications of the π_1(X, p(x)).
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group with simply connected base region / 'base point = contractible or simply connected region'; related to fundamental groupoid on a set of base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; R. Brown (groupoids on sets of base points, 1960s); used systematically by Deligne (1989) and Ihara school, e.g. real intervals, upper half-plane
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in SGA1 (fibre functors, groupoids) and Esquisse d'un programme (groupoids with well-chosen base points); this exact device unsure

ideas.what: Galois cocycle g_{y,x}(u) = defect of Galois invariance of the canonical path between two K-rational points x, y lying in a common simply connected region, satisfying g_{zy} g_{yx} = g_{zx}.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale path torsors / path cocycles σ ↦ σ(γ)γ^{-1}; 'Chasles' relation

ideas.what: Recovering ordinary path cocycles as the case T = [0,1], and functoriality in T over X (continued on next page).

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, apparently around 1978–81, the formalism of Galois cocycles attached to pairs of rational points in a simply connected 'base region' T → X, with π_1(X;T) as a canonical common receptacle and the Chasles identity g_{zy}g_{yx}=g_{zx}. This predates or parallels the Ihara/Deligne/Nakamura use of real intervals and tangential base points. The neighbouring page adds 'chemins infinitésimaux', a germ of tangential base points.
missed.quote: Soit T un espace topologique 1-connexe, et p : T → X ... π = π_1(X;T) ... g^{T/X}_{y,x}(u) = φ_y^{-1}(g_{l_{y,x}}(u)) = φ_x^{-1}(f_{l_{y,x}}(u))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority: it documents Grothendieck working with base regions and infinitesimal paths for Galois actions on π̂_1 before Deligne's 1989 tangential base points. Mathematically the content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is natural and now standard (base regions, path torsors, Galois path cocycles). Its interest is historical: an early, explicit Grothendieck formulation in the anabelian/Teichmüller context, adjacent to a germ of tangential base points.
transcription_corrections: First line should read '(9) de passage de f à g, sous une forme considérablement plus simple' (not 'du groupe de f : g'). The next page refers back to 'formules de passage (9)'. The isolated '4' at top is a page number.
In (14) the crossed-out start is an aborted 'π_1(X;T'; the retained formula is π_1(X;T) = π (lowercase π_1, as at the bottom of the page).
Parenthetical after (13) is largely illegible; likely a remark that the surjectivity condition on π_0 is the most restrictive, or similar. Do not trust the machine reading.
Margin note probably: 'On désignera aussi par π_1(X;T) le groupe [π] ... défini par les isos (15)' / 'à isomorphisme unique près'.
